Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:4759
Court No. - 12
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 13800 of 2023

Applicant :- Irfan
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt., Govt. Civil Secrt. Lko.

An
Counsel for Applicant :- Mohd.Mateen,Dharmendra Kumar Tripathi,Shailendra Pathak
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
Despite service of notice, no one appeared on behalf of the complainant.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.245 of 2023, under Sections 366, 376, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Balrampur.

3. In terms of the FIR filed through an application under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C., it was alleged that on 04.07.2023, the daughter of the informant was enticed away by the applicant and was wanted to take her at Bombay.
Somehow, she was caught at the railway station.
In the statement Irfan vs State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181936697/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., it was stated that on the false pretext of marriage, the applicant formed physical relation with her.
She also stated that the applicant was stayed as a neighbour and used to harass her.
It was also stated that he used to tell her that he would marry and on 04.07.2023, he took her on a motorcycle and thereafter rape was committed.
In the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she reiterated the said version.
Although she stated that she was in love with the applicant and had gone on the false pretext of marriage.
4. In the light of the aforesaid, the Counsel for the applicant is that FIR itself was lodged after about 16 days of the alleged incident.
He further argues that in the medical report on record, no injuries was visible to corroborate the allegations levelled in the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
As regards the age, it is argued that as per the Pariwar Register, the age of the victim is around 25 years whereas Class-VIII certificate shows her age to be around 17 years.
5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

6. Considering the variance in the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. and the fact that prima facie the allegation does not corroborate with the medical report on record; there is no definite documents with regard to the age of victim, which is to be seen at the time of trail coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is in custody since 01.08.2023, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Irfan be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
